Rab14 reduced cell membrane expression of UT-A1

Rab14 overexpression reduced lipid droplet number and volume
Rab14 overexpression inhibited PLIN2 expression
Rab14 overexpression inhibited AKT phosphorylation and induced granulosa cell apoptosis

model_organism.citation: MIR144 and MIR451 regulate human erythropoiesis via RAB14. (PMID: 25312678)
phenotypes: MIR451 inhibition resulted in decreased erythroid cell numbers (consistent with prior zebrafish studies)
RAB14 identified as direct target of MIR144 and MIR451 in erythropoiesis context
RAB14 knockdown increased frequency and number of erythroid cells
RAB14 knockdown increased beta-haemoglobin expression
RAB14 knockdown decreased CBFA2T3 expression

biological.summary: Rab14 knockdown caused mitochondria to acquire elongated morphology and increased mitochondrial protein levels, while Rab14 overexpression decreased these proteins and increased mitophagy as shown by mito-Keima assays. Rab14-induced mitophagy was dependent on Parkin, TBK1, and PI3K activity, placing it in the Parkin-dependent mitophagy pathway. 3D reconstruction showed contact site formation between Rab14 and mitochondria, mediated by TGN-derived Rab14 vesicles.

biological.citation: Biogenesis of Rab14-positive endosome buds at Golgi-endosome contacts by the RhoBTB3-SHIP164-Vps26B complex. (PMID: 38565878)
biological.summary: Vps26B was identified as a novel Rab14 effector, and Rab14 activity regulates the association of SHIP164 with early endosomes. Depletion of SHIP164 leads to enlarged Rab14+ early endosomes without buds, and Rab14 activity is essential for the RhoBTB3-SHIP164-Vps26B complex-mediated lipid transport-dependent pathway at Golgi-EE contacts required for endosome budding.

biological.citation: Rab14 Overexpression Promotes Proliferation and Invasion Through YAP Signaling in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancers. (PMID: 32982313)
biological.summary: Rab14 was upregulated in 65 of 115 NSCLC tissues and correlated with advanced TNM stage and nodal metastasis. Rab14 overexpression increased proliferation, invasion, and cell cycle progression while activating YAP signaling by stabilizing YAP protein and increasing nuclear YAP accumulation. YAP knockdown abolished the effects of Rab14 on cyclin D1, cyclin E, CTGF, cell proliferation, and invasion.
biological.sample_size: 115 NSCLC tissue cases; 6 cancer cell lines

biological.citation: MIR144 and MIR451 regulate human erythropoiesis via RAB14. (PMID: 25312678)
biological.summary: RAB14 was identified as a direct target of both MIR144 and MIR451 during human erythropoiesis; as these miRNAs increased during erythropoiesis, RAB14 protein expression decreased. Enforced RAB14 expression phenocopied the inhibitory effect of MIR144/MIR451 depletion on erythroid differentiation, while shRNA-mediated RAB14 knockdown increased erythroid cell frequency, β-haemoglobin expression, and decreased CBFA2T3, identifying RAB14 as a physiological inhibitor of human erythropoiesis.

biological.citation: PKCι interacts with Rab14 and modulates epithelial barrier function through regulation of claudin-2 levels. (PMID: 25694446)
biological.summary: PKCι and Rab14 (a TGN/endosomal small GTPase) interact directly as shown by ELISA and coimmunoprecipitation, and colocalize in intracellular puncta and at the plasma membrane. Rab14 expression is required for normal PKCι distribution in 3D cyst culture, and together they regulate trafficking of claudin-2 out of the lysosome-directed pathway, thereby modulating epithelial barrier function and transepithelial resistance.

biological.citation: Rab14/MACF2 complex regulates endosomal targeting during cytokinesis. (PMID: 33566684)
biological.summary: Rab14 was identified as a novel regulator of cytokinesis; its depletion caused cytokinesis failure or significantly prolonged division time. Rab14 contributes to recruiting Rab11-endosomes to intracellular bridge microtubules and its knockout inhibits actin clearance at the abscission site. Rab14 binds the microtubule minus-end interacting MACF2/CAMSAP3 complex, and this binding affects endosome targeting to intracellular bridge microtubules.

biological.citation: Targeting CPT1A-mediated fatty acid oxidation sensitizes nasopharyngeal carcinoma to radiation therapy. (PMID: 29721083)
biological.summary: Rab14 was identified as a novel CPT1A-binding protein via liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, confirmed by immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence, and proximity ligation assay. The CPT1A-Rab14 interaction facilitated fatty acid trafficking from lipid droplets to mitochondria, decreasing radiation-induced lipid accumulation and maximizing ATP production. Knockdown of Rab14 attenuated CPT1A-mediated fatty acid trafficking and radiation resistance in NPC cells.

biological.citation: The Small GTPase Rab14 Regulates the Trafficking of Ceramide from Endoplasmic Reticulum to Golgi Apparatus and Facilitates Classical Swine Fever Virus Assembly. (PMID: 37255314)
biological.summary: Rab14 knockdown and overexpression significantly affected CSFV replication, particularly at the late stage of infection. CSFV NS5A recruited Rab14 to the ER to facilitate ceramide transport to the Golgi apparatus for sphingomyelin synthesis, which was required for viral particle assembly. The PI3K/AKT/AS160 signaling pathway regulated Rab14 function in ceramide transport, and blockage of this pathway reduced sphingomyelin content and impaired virus assembly.

biological.citation: Rab14 is overexpressed in ovarian cancers and promotes ovarian cancer proliferation through Wnt pathway. (PMID: 27718127)
biological.summary: Rab14 was overexpressed in ovarian cancer specimens and its overexpression correlated with FIGO stage. Rab14 overexpression regulated GSK3β phosphorylation and nuclear β-catenin accumulation, enhanced TCF transcriptional activity, and upregulated Wnt target genes MMP7 and c-myc, while a Wnt inhibitor abolished these effects. Rab14 knockdown inhibited cell growth and invasion while overexpression facilitated them and increased paclitaxel resistance.

biological.citation: Rab14-Mediated Lipophagy Disrupts Lipid Homeostasis in Granulosa Cells and Impairs Female Fertility. (PMID: 41553083)
biological.summary: Rab14 expression was upregulated in granulosa cells following peri-ovarian adipose tissue removal in a mouse model, which was associated with impaired follicle development and increased apoptosis. Rab14 overexpression significantly enhanced lipophagy activity, reduced lipid droplet number and volume, inhibited PLIN2 expression, and inhibited AKT phosphorylation, inducing granulosa cell apoptosis. These findings link Rab14-mediated lipophagy to disrupted lipid homeostasis and impaired female fertility.
